summary: Wave D-1 F2 (docs/WAVE_D_FEEDBACK.md: the liquid must look more like a DROP) is implemented and checked on Build/liq-drop. (1) A dome field: TerritoryField builds _PIO_TerritoryDome in the same scissored command buffer as the territory blur. TerritoryBlur passes 6-8 are appended after the unchanged passes 0-5: the visual mask is box-downsampled and blurred with a Gaussian of sigma 0.8 u on a 256 x 256 grid (21 + 11 taps), then B-spline reconstructed into a mask-sized RGBA half texture. It holds t_dome (max over the channels), its world gradient, and t_dome sampled 0.32 u toward the key light for the shadow. It has its own render textures and a wider dirty rectangle (32 cells), so the scissored path stays exact: after a fill the dome under the capture rises and a far region reads back bit for bit unchanged (EditMode GPU read-back test). (2) LiquidComposite takes one extra fetch, the F2 allowance (B-spline on High). The narrow meniscus keeps its crisp bevel and its edge streaks (PIO_ShadeLiquid unchanged). The dome adds its own layer. The depth (bevel x C(2 t_dome - 1)) is 0 on the edge and on thin strips and 1 in a thick center 1.5 - 2 u inside. On top of that: depth absorption (albedo^0.88 at the thin rim to albedo^1.14 in the thick center, so a lighter translucent edge and a richer body), a wrapped Lambert of the dome normal (the body is lit from the upper left and turns deeper on the lower right), a broad soft highlight band plus a sharp hot spot, and a softer, stronger contact shadow on the lower right from the dome's shadow channel. All of this runs on every tier with no extra fetch; the per-pixel drop terms run only inside the puddle and actor branches. Actors on their own puddle take the same terms (no seam at necks or around a pearl at home); threads on bare ground or on rival puddles are unchanged. LiquidTheme.DropStrength (1, published as _PIO_BiomeParams.x) scales everything; 0 gives back the wave C puddles. (3) Bead.hlsl: a pearl-sized bead that moves becomes a slight teardrop along its motion (rear half 28 % longer and tapered toward its thread), and its shadow follows. Droplets, splash drops and the retraction bulb bead keep their shapes. (4) LiquidCommon.hlsl: additions only, and its two functions are byte for byte unchanged (hash-checked). Checks: SetupAndCompile PASS (ShaderCheck 12 shaders, 0 failure) and BuildWindows PASS. EditMode: 503 tests, 500 passing, 2 skipped (pre-existing BotTests) and 1 failing on purpose: WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount still expects 13 LiquidComposite fetch sites and now finds 14 (see needs). That run includes 10 new WaveD_ tests, among them the GPU read-back of the dome and the GLES3x + D3D11 compile of every TerritoryBlur pass and of the LiquidComposite and Bead forward passes; a filtered re-run on the final sources gave 42 tests with the same single failure. PlayMode 8/8. The release probe hash is 246577239DE179C4 at -fps 30 and 144 (PASS). Visuals: before (gate C Build/Windows) and after (final Build/liq-drop) DevShots at 540x960 and 1080x2400 in High and Medium, plus RenderLab in High, Medium and Low, side by side with docs/reference_gouttes.png under docs/waveD/shots/liq-drop/compare/. Every puddle now reads as one domed drop. V1-V8 hold, and the median puddle colors stay within 9 sRGB levels of the palette with unchanged saturation. The fill wave domes up as it fills and the evaporation still fades the puddle. Fire is unchanged (pixel diffs at the run-to-run noise floor). Electric differs only by the F3 interior arcs of the elec-arcs package, which are in the same source tree; its ground pixels are identical. Perf (verify.ps1 -Steps perfslope, Medium, uncapped, best of 2 rounds, quiet runs): liquid went from 1.84 ms/Mpix on the gate C build (1080x1200 3.20 ms, 540x600 1.41 ms) to 1.94 ms/Mpix on the final build (3.27 / 1.38 ms), +5.4 %, within the +15 % limit; the step PASSes (fire/liquid 1.41, electric/liquid 1.20, hash unchanged). An interleaved, locked A/B of 4 rounds (all quiet) gave 1.94 vs 2.13 ms/Mpix (+9.8 %), and 3.15 vs 3.26 ms at 1080x1200 (+3.5 %). A first build that evaluated the drop terms on every pixel measured 2.20 (+19.6 %), which is why they moved into the branches.

contract_issues: 12.2 item 1 (territory field): add a third field, the dome. TerritoryField also publishes _PIO_TerritoryDome (mask-sized, field format: x = t_dome = max over the channels of a Gaussian of sigma 0.8 u of the visual mask, yz = its world gradient, w = t_dome sampled PIO_DOME_SHADOW_REACH = 0.32 u toward the key light) and _PIO_TerritoryDomeTexel. TerritoryBlur builds it in the same command buffer with three passes: 6 DomeH (2 x 2 box down to a 256 grid plus a 21-tap Gaussian along x), 7 DomeV (11 linear taps along y) and 8 DomeField (B-spline reconstruction, central-difference gradient, shadow sample). It has its own render textures (two 256 grids and the mask-sized output) and its own dirty rectangle, grown by DomeGrowCells = 32 cells (the 12.2 'grown by 4 sigma + 2 cells' rule applied to the dome kernel). Passes 0-5 and _PIO_TerritoryField / _PIO_TerritoryHeight are unchanged.

12.2 item 4 and 26.9 (fetch budget): Medium is now 8 fetches without actors and 12 with actors (was 7 / 11; 12 is the original 12.2 item 4 cap), and Low is 6 / 10 (was 5 / 9). The difference is the one dome fetch allowed by F2. High samples the dome with the B-spline helper (4 taps). WaveC_Composites_KeepTheirFetchCount must read 14 LiquidComposite fetch sites (see needs).

12.2 item 3 (composite shading), add the drop layer: depth = (HT / h0) x C(2 t_dome - 1), with C(q) = 1.15 q^2 / (q + 0.15). The albedo becomes albedo^e, with e from 0.88 (thin rim, thin strips) to 1.14 (thick center). The dome normal (lighting slope 0.45 x b x C'(q) x 2 grad t_dome) feeds a wrapped Lambert, a broad band (Blinn lobe of power 10 toward the key light's half vector, strength 0.7, sheen 60 % toward white) and a hot spot (power 900 around a half vector tilted 12 degrees toward the light). The ground contact shadow is 0.35 x smoothstep(0.2, 0.8, t_dome toward the light), on every tier. PIO_ShadeLiquid still shades the meniscus with the relief normal, unchanged. An actor on its own puddle takes the drop terms weighted by own; threads on bare ground or a rival puddle do not. _PIO_BiomeParams.x (LiquidTheme.DropStrength = 1) scales the layer; 0 gives back the wave C puddles.

12.3 Pearl and 12.3 Beads: 'while trailing, the bead keeps its full round silhouette' becomes 'keeps its full silhouette (never absorbed early)'. Per F2, a moving pearl (bead radius >= 0.3 u, PearlView stretch > 1) is drawn as a slight teardrop along its motion: the rear half is up to 28 % longer and narrows toward the thread (Bead.hlsl PIO_TearWarp). It is full at the steady MovingStretch 1.04 and absent when the pearl squashes in a tight turn, and its shadow follows. Droplets, splash drops and the retraction bulb bead (all below 0.3 u) are unchanged.
25.2 BiomeTheme: the Liquide theme's ShaderParams is (DropStrength, 0, 0, 0); x is the drop strength read by LiquidComposite (it was zero).

12.5: suggested V9 for F2: 'every puddle reads as one domed drop: its body keeps rising for 1.5 - 2 u from the edge, a broad soft highlight band and a sharp hot spot sit on the upper left, the thick center is richer and the thin rim lighter, the meniscus foot stays crisp, and a soft contact shadow falls on the lower right; a moving pearl is a slight teardrop'.

open_issues: Electric invariance cannot be shown by a plain screenshot diff. Build/liq-drop compiles the shared tree, which already holds the elec-arcs package's F3 interior arcs (ElectricComposite.hlsl, ElectricTheme.ShaderParams), and the electric shots differ from gate C exactly where those arcs are (compare/invariance_fire_electric.png). Ground pixels (luma < 60, 70 - 91 % of the frame) differ on 0.000 - 0.07 % of pixels, which is within the noise floor of two gate C runs (0.000 - 0.14 %). Structurally, neither the electric nor the fire composite can change. They never read the dome (WaveD_OtherBiomeShaders_NeverReadTheDome). TerritoryBlur passes 0-5 and their helpers are byte for byte those of wave C (hash-checked). TerritoryField's first six passes and their textures are untouched. LiquidCommon only gained declarations the other shaders do not use, and the compiler strips them.

DevShot run-to-run noise: fire and electric use time-animated noise, and the render interpolation of the capture frame varies, so two runs of the same build can differ by a sub-pixel offset of the whole frame. For example, fire Medium ThreadOut differs by 4.1 % of pixels between two runs of Build/liq-drop, and by 0.006 % between two runs of the gate C build. Runs with matching timing compare at the floor: fire ThreadOut gate C vs build 1 was 0.006 % (Medium) and 0.007 % (High), and MidFill was 0.47 % / 0.025 %. Liquid shows the same effect through the wobble and the drifting pocket stripes: two builds with identical liquid math (build 1 and the final build differ only in where the drop terms are evaluated) compare at 0.000 % on 1080x2400 Medium ThreadOut and at up to 7 % on shots with moving stripes.

The dome follows the visual mask, so wave D-2's TerritoryGrew fill (treated as a fill from the edge) will dome up the grown ring with no dome change. Scorched cells need nothing either, because the scorch mask darkens the composite on top.

The perf numbers come from a shared laptop (Iris Xe). The official run of the final build had 12 quiet runs, but its 540x600 size was noisy (x1.3 between rounds), as 26.7 warns. The gate's quiet-machine run should confirm them.

DevShot and RenderLab take the human's color from the shared PlayerPrefs. I pinned pio.ColorIndex to 0 (coral, the 26.3 measurement rule) for every run, from its earlier value of 2, and set it back to 2 at the end. In the first parallel batch, one RenderLab Low capture came out as an unrelated scene with a saffron human while another agent's player was running. A rerun on its own was correct, and that rerun is the one kept.

Transparency: at the start I copied my seven owned files into the shared scratchpad folder orig/ before noticing that it belonged to a finished wave C agent. That overwrote its old backups of LiquidCommon.hlsl and LiquidComposite.hlsl (wave C sources dated 16:10, superseded by the gate C tree). My backups and scripts are now under scratchpad/liq-drop/. I also briefly created a stray C:/Dev/squad-ai/Brainstorming/scratchpad_dummy.png through a bad relative path and deleted it at once.
